This way, the model doesn’t have to rely solely on its internal knowledge but can access whatever data you provide it at the right time. The model is therefore better equipped to provide more accurate and contextually appropriate responses, by incorporating proprietary data stored in a database that offers vector search as a feature. data.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems
data.content:
## Conclusion

While RAG significantly reduces the hallucination rate of LLMs, it does not eliminate it entirely. A layered approach that strengthens retrieval, structures generation, enforces source fidelity, and verifies outputs is essential. As LLMs continue to integrate with mission-critical applications, rigorous hallucination mitigation will be pivotal for trustworthy AI.

> _Learn more about prompt engineering:__OpenAI Prompting Guide_ [...] ## Understanding Hallucinations in RAG

RAG systems retrieve relevant documents from a knowledge base and use them to condition the response of an LLM. However, hallucinations may still occur due to:

1.   Retrieval Errors: Irrelevant or outdated documents retrieved.
2.   Insufficient Conditioning: The LLM underutilizes retrieved context.
3.   Generative Overreach: LLMs extrapolate or fabricate details not grounded in the retrieval context.
